arc: One second of eye contact to the thing you have not been saying.

tiers.do: Make eye contact with one stranger. One second. That is the entire task.
tiers.why: One second. No smile required, no words. Contact, then look away.
tiers.alt: Look up from your phone whenever someone passes you today.
tiers.when: I next pass someone on the pavement
tiers.open: Lift your eyes off the pavement before the next person reaches you.
tiers.done: one stranger's eyes met yours for about a second.
tiers.test: them to look away disgusted, or to say something to you.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Say thank you out loud, with eye contact, to someone who serves you.
tiers.why: You already say it. Today you say it to a face.
tiers.alt: Say good morning to one person you pass regularly.
tiers.when: I am next handed my change or my receipt
tiers.open: Look up before you take the change, not after.
tiers.done: you said it out loud, to a face, and they heard it.
tiers.test: your voice to come out wrong and the moment to be awkward.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.
tiers.say: "Thank you — have a good one."

tiers.do: Ask one stranger a question with a factual answer. "Is this the queue?"
tiers.why: A question you already know the answer to is still a door opened.
tiers.alt: Ask someone the time, even with your phone in your pocket.
tiers.when: I next join the back of a queue
tiers.open: Turn your head toward the nearest person before you lose the nerve.
tiers.done: you asked, they answered, and you said thank you.
tiers.test: them to look at you like the question was stupid.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "Sorry — is this the queue for the till?"

tiers.do: Hold a door for someone and say something as they pass.
tiers.why: A gesture plus three words. That is the whole increment.
tiers.alt: Let someone go ahead of you and say something about it.
tiers.when: I next put my hand on a door someone else is about to come through
tiers.open: Put your hand on the door and hold it.
tiers.done: you held it and said something out loud as they passed.
tiers.test: them to go through without acknowledging you at all.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "After you. It is heavier than it looks."

tiers.do: Compliment a stranger on something they chose. Shoes, bag, jacket.
tiers.why: Chosen things only, never bodies. Then leave. No follow-up needed.
tiers.alt: Compliment someone you know on a specific choice they made.
tiers.when: I next pass someone on the pavement
tiers.open: Notice one thing somebody chose, not something about their body.
tiers.done: you said it, they heard it, and you kept walking.
tiers.test: them to think you want something, or to be creeped out.
tiers.stop: Do not prepare an exit line before you start.
tiers.say: "Those are good — where are they from?" Then go.

tiers.do: Answer a question with more than the minimum today.
tiers.why: 'Fine' is a wall. Add one sentence behind it.
tiers.alt: Give one honest answer where you would normally deflect.
tiers.when: someone next asks me how I am
tiers.open: Answer, then add one more sentence before you stop talking.
tiers.done: one answer today had a real sentence behind the first word.
tiers.test: them to be bored, or to wonder why you are telling them.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Make a phone call you would rather send as a message.
tiers.why: Voice removes the edit button. That is the exercise.
tiers.alt: Send a voice note where you would have typed.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Open the contact and press call instead of typing.
tiers.done: the call happened and you spoke rather than typed.
tiers.test: to stumble, go blank, and sound strange on the phone.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.

tiers.do: Sit among people for thirty minutes — a bench, a square, a library.
tiers.why: Ambient presence. You are not talking to anyone, just available to.
tiers.alt: Sit in a café for twenty minutes with no headphones.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Sit down and put your phone in your pocket.
tiers.done: thirty minutes passed among people with the phone away.
tiers.test: to be stared at, or approached, for sitting there doing nothing.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Ask someone working — driver, librarian, receptionist — how their shift is going. Wait for the answer.
tiers.why: The waiting is the challenge. Most people leave before it arrives.
tiers.alt: Ask whoever serves you a real question and listen to all of it.
tiers.when: I next reach the front of a till
tiers.open: Ask, then stay still and wait for the whole answer.
tiers.done: you waited through the pause and heard the actual answer.
tiers.test: them to give you nothing, and for the pause to be unbearable.
tiers.stop: Do not prepare an exit line before you start.
tiers.say: "How is the shift going?" Then wait.

tiers.do: Say something unprompted to a neighbour or colleague.
tiers.why: Starting is harder than continuing. Practise the start.
tiers.alt: Speak first to someone you usually wait for.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Speak before they do. One sentence is enough.
tiers.done: you spoke first, unprompted, to someone you did not have to.
tiers.test: them to be surprised, or to not want the conversation.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "Morning. Busy one today?"

tiers.do: Ask a stranger for a small recommendation and take it.
tiers.why: Asking makes you briefly dependent. That is the muscle.
tiers.alt: Ask a staff member what they would choose, and choose it.
tiers.when: I next reach the front of a till
tiers.open: Ask them to choose for you, then take what they say.
tiers.done: you asked, and you actually took the recommendation.
tiers.test: them to be annoyed at being asked to do your thinking.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "I do not know what to get — what would you have?"

tiers.do: Reply properly to one message you have been leaving unanswered.
tiers.why: Avoidance costs more than the conversation ever would.
tiers.alt: Answer the message you have reread and not replied to.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Open the message you have been avoiding and write the first line.
tiers.done: the reply is sent and it answers what they actually asked.
tiers.test: them to be angry about how long you took.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "Sorry for the slow reply — no good reason. How are you?"

tiers.do: Give someone your full attention for ten minutes. No phone.
tiers.why: Undivided attention is rare enough to be a gift.
tiers.alt: Have one conversation with your phone out of reach.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Put the phone face down and out of reach before they start talking.
tiers.done: ten minutes of conversation happened with no phone in it.
tiers.test: to run out of things to say and for the silence to be obvious.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Sit in a café for one hour. No headphones, no phone.
tiers.why: Available, unarmoured, in public. Nothing else required.
tiers.alt: Spend forty minutes in a public space with no devices.
tiers.when: I next pay for a coffee
tiers.open: Order, sit down, and leave your phone and headphones in your bag.
tiers.done: an hour passed in public with nothing to hide behind.
tiers.test: to be visibly alone for an hour and to be pitied for it.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Ask someone a question about themselves and one follow-up.
tiers.why: The follow-up is what separates interest from politeness.
tiers.alt: Ask one person two questions in a row about their life.
tiers.when: someone next asks me how I am
tiers.open: Ask them something about themselves, then ask about their answer.
tiers.done: you asked a second question that came out of their first answer.
tiers.test: them to think you are prying, or to give one-word answers.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "How did you end up doing that?" Then: "What is the part you like?"

tiers.do: Speak to someone at least twenty years older or younger than you.
tiers.why: Age-segregated lives are smaller lives.
tiers.alt: Have a real exchange with someone from another generation.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Speak to the person whose age makes you hesitate.
tiers.done: a real exchange happened with someone a generation away from you.
tiers.test: to have nothing in common and for it to be visibly awkward.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.

tiers.do: Tell someone one true thing about your day, unasked.
tiers.why: Volunteering something small is how closeness starts.
tiers.alt: Share one honest detail nobody asked you for.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say one true thing about your day before they ask.
tiers.done: you volunteered something true that nobody asked for.
tiers.test: them to not care, and for you to feel exposed for offering it.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Eat at a counter, bar, or shared table rather than alone.
tiers.why: Proximity without obligation. Good practice ground.
tiers.alt: Sit at a shared table somewhere instead of a solo one.
tiers.when: I finish eating lunch tomorrow
tiers.open: Ask for a seat at the bar or the shared table, not a booth.
tiers.done: you ate at a shared surface with strangers either side.
tiers.test: to be squeezed in, awkward, and to want to leave.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.
tiers.say: "Is it alright if I sit here?"

tiers.do: Say no to something you would normally accept.
tiers.why: A boundary is a social skill, not a social cost.
tiers.alt: Decline one request without an elaborate excuse.
tiers.when: someone next asks me how I am
tiers.open: Say the word no first, before any explanation.
tiers.done: you declined, and you did not build an excuse around it.
tiers.test: them to be offended, and for it to cost you the relationship.
tiers.stop: Do not explain yourself. No reasons, no justification — the sentence stands alone.
tiers.say: "No, I cannot do that one." Then stop.

tiers.do: Hold a conversation with a stranger for three full exchanges.
tiers.why: Three exchanges is where small talk dies or becomes something.
tiers.alt: Keep any unplanned conversation going past the natural exit.
tiers.when: I next join the back of a queue
tiers.open: Say the first thing. Then stay in the conversation past the second.
tiers.done: three full back-and-forths happened before it ended.
tiers.test: it to dry up after one exchange and to stand there in silence.
tiers.stop: Do not prepare an exit line before you start.

tiers.do: Ask someone for help you could technically manage alone.
tiers.why: Needing people is not a weakness you have to hide.
tiers.alt: Let someone help you with something you would normally refuse.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask for the help you do not strictly need.
tiers.done: someone helped you with something you could have done alone.
tiers.test: them to think you are incapable, or to resent being asked.
tiers.stop: Do not explain yourself. No reasons, no justification — the sentence stands alone.
tiers.say: "Could you give me a hand with this?"

tiers.do: Pay someone a compliment about who they are, not what they did.
tiers.why: Character compliments land harder and cost more to give.
tiers.alt: Tell someone one thing you genuinely admire about them.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say what they are like, not what they did.
tiers.done: you told someone something about their character, to their face.
tiers.test: it to land as strange, or too much, and for them to deflect.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "You are very steady about things. I notice it."

tiers.do: Speak to a stranger while waiting somewhere. Queue, platform, lift.
tiers.why: Dead time is the easiest opening you will ever get.
tiers.alt: Start one conversation in a place where you are both waiting.
tiers.when: I am next standing at a stop or a platform
tiers.open: Say something about where you both are. That is the whole opener.
tiers.done: a conversation happened with a stranger while you were both waiting.
tiers.test: them to be irritated at being spoken to.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "Any idea how long these usually take?"

tiers.do: Have one conversation where you talk less than half the time.
tiers.why: Listening is the half of this most people never train.
tiers.alt: Ask more questions than you make statements, once today.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Ask the first question, then count your own sentences.
tiers.done: you talked less than half the time and you know you did.
tiers.test: to be boring, and for the conversation to die because you held back.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Introduce yourself to someone whose name you have never learned.
tiers.why: You have shared space for months. Learn the name.
tiers.alt: Learn the name of someone you see regularly and use it.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask their name. Nothing else needs to happen.
tiers.done: you know the name and you have used it out loud once.
tiers.test: them to be insulted that you never asked before.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "I realised I have never asked your name. I am ——."

tiers.do: Invite someone for something specific with a day and a time.
tiers.why: 'We should catch up' is not an invitation. A date and time is.
tiers.alt: Send one invitation containing an actual time.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Name a day and a time in the message before you send it.
tiers.done: an invitation went out with an actual day and time in it.
tiers.test: them to say no, or to leave it on read.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "Are you free Thursday evening? I was thinking about ——."

tiers.do: Disagree out loud, calmly, with something said in front of you.
tiers.why: Agreeable silence is a habit, not a personality.
tiers.alt: State one honest, mild disagreement instead of nodding.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say the disagreement out loud, calmly, before the moment passes.
tiers.done: you said you disagreed and you did not take it back.
tiers.test: them to be angry, and for the room to turn against you.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "I see it differently, actually."

tiers.do: Text someone you have drifted from. Propose a specific day.
tiers.why: The specific day is the task. Vagueness is how drift continues.
tiers.alt: Reach out to one person you have lost touch with.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Open the drifted contact and write the date into the first line.
tiers.done: the message is sent and it contains a specific day.
tiers.test: them to have moved on and to not want to hear from you.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "This is overdue. Are you about on the ——? I would like to catch up properly."

tiers.do: Spend an evening with people without checking your phone once.
tiers.why: Presence is measurable. Measure it tonight.
tiers.alt: Spend two hours with people, phone away entirely.
tiers.when: I turn the lights on this evening
tiers.open: Put your phone in your coat before you walk in.
tiers.done: the whole evening passed without you checking once.
tiers.test: to be anxious all evening about what you are missing.
tiers.stop: Phone stays in your pocket. Holding it to look busy is the thing to drop.

tiers.do: Ask someone about the hardest part of their week.
tiers.why: Past the weather, into the actual life. One question does it.
tiers.alt: Ask one person a question they will have to think about.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Ask the question, then say nothing at all.
tiers.done: you asked about the hard part and they answered it.
tiers.test: them to be uncomfortable and to shut the question down.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "What has been the hardest part of your week?"

tiers.do: Say the thing you were going to leave unsaid in a small conversation.
tiers.why: Practise on low stakes. The high stakes are coming.
tiers.alt: Voice one small thought you would normally swallow.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say the thing you were about to swallow.
tiers.done: the small unsaid thing was said out loud.
tiers.test: it to be unwelcome, and for the mood to change.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Go to a group event alone. Speak to two people.
tiers.why: Arriving alone removes the exit. That is the mechanism.
tiers.alt: Attend anything social by yourself and speak to one person.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find one event this week and go without asking anyone to come.
tiers.done: you arrived alone and spoke to two separate people.
tiers.test: to stand at the edge all evening and speak to nobody.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.
tiers.say: "Mind if I join you? I came on my own."

tiers.do: Join a conversation you were not part of.
tiers.why: Entering uninvited is a skill and it is rarely unwelcome.
tiers.alt: Step into one group conversation today.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Move into the group and say something about what they are discussing.
tiers.done: you joined a conversation you were not part of and stayed in it.
tiers.test: them to stop talking, look at you, and wait for you to leave.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "Sorry — I overheard. Is that the one where ——?"

tiers.do: Tell someone you appreciate them, specifically, to their face.
tiers.why: Specific and spoken. Written is easier, which is why it is not the task.
tiers.alt: Thank someone properly, out loud, for something specific.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say it to their face. Not in writing.
tiers.done: you told them, out loud, specifically what you appreciate.
tiers.test: it to be awkward, and for them to not know what to say.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "I want to say — the thing you did about —— mattered. Thank you."

tiers.do: Spend two hours with someone whose views differ from yours.
tiers.why: Stay curious for two hours. You do not have to agree.
tiers.alt: Have one long conversation with someone you disagree with.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Ask the person you disagree with for two hours of their time.
tiers.done: two hours passed and you stayed curious without conceding.
tiers.test: it to become an argument you cannot get out of.
tiers.stop: Do not prepare an exit line before you start.
tiers.say: "I do not see it that way, but I want to understand how you do."

tiers.do: Ask two people for their contact details in one week.
tiers.why: Collecting is the easy half. Get comfortable with the ask.
tiers.alt: Ask one person for a way to stay in touch.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask the first person this week, not the easiest one.
tiers.done: two people gave you a way to contact them inside one week.
tiers.test: them to hesitate, make an excuse, and for you to have read it wrong.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "Can I take your number? I would like to do this again."

tiers.do: Organise something small for three people.
tiers.why: You become responsible for the room. New skill entirely.
tiers.alt: Arrange a meet-up for two other people and yourself.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Pick the date first, then message the three people.
tiers.done: three people turned up to the thing you arranged.
tiers.test: nobody to come, or for it to be flat and awkward.
tiers.stop: No escape arranged in advance. No pre-booked way out.

tiers.do: Have a conversation about something that actually matters to you.
tiers.why: Depth is a choice available in most conversations. Take it.
tiers.alt: Steer one conversation to something you genuinely care about.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Steer it once, deliberately, toward the thing you care about.
tiers.done: one conversation went past small talk into something that matters to you.
tiers.test: them to be uninterested and to steer it back.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Apologise properly for something you have been avoiding.
tiers.why: No qualifiers, no explanation of why you were right.
tiers.alt: Apologise once without adding a defence.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say sorry, name the thing, and stop talking.
tiers.done: the apology was given with no explanation attached to it.
tiers.test: them to not accept it, and for you to have made it worse.
tiers.stop: Do not explain yourself. No reasons, no justification — the sentence stands alone.
tiers.say: "I am sorry about ——. There is no excuse for it."

tiers.do: Get a stranger's contact and follow up within forty-eight hours.
tiers.why: The follow-up is the tier. Collecting and never using it is tier 36.
tiers.alt: Follow up with someone new within two days of meeting them.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Get the number. Then put a reminder in for tomorrow.
tiers.done: you made contact again inside forty-eight hours.
tiers.test: them to not reply, and for the silence to be the answer.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "Good to meet you yesterday. Fancy a coffee this week?"

tiers.do: Attend something alone where you know nobody at all.
tiers.why: No familiar faces, no exit strategy. Stay the whole time.
tiers.alt: Go somewhere social where you have no existing connection.
tiers.when: I close my laptop at the end of the day
tiers.open: Find the thing where you know nobody and commit to the whole evening.
tiers.done: you stayed for the whole thing in a room of strangers.
tiers.test: to know nobody, talk to nobody, and leave early.
tiers.stop: Go alone. Bringing someone turns it into a different task.

tiers.do: Ask someone to teach you something they are good at.
tiers.why: Admitting ignorance and asking is a double exposure.
tiers.alt: Ask one person to show you their skill.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Ask the person who is good at it to show you.
tiers.done: somebody taught you something and you were the one who asked.
tiers.test: them to think you are wasting their time.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "You are good at ——. Would you show me how you do it?"

tiers.do: Have a conversation you have been dreading.
tiers.why: Dread is interest rate. The longer you wait the more it costs.
tiers.alt: Start the conversation you keep postponing.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Say the first sentence of the conversation you have been dreading.
tiers.done: the dreaded conversation happened, start to finish.
tiers.test: it to go exactly as badly as you have been imagining.
tiers.stop: Do not rehearse the sentence. Say the first version that arrives.
tiers.say: "There is something I need to say and I have been putting it off."

tiers.do: Spend a full day saying yes to every reasonable invitation.
tiers.why: Your default is no. Try the other default for one day.
tiers.alt: Accept every invitation you receive this week.
tiers.when: I first get out of bed tomorrow morning
tiers.open: Say yes to the first invitation before you weigh it up.
tiers.done: every reasonable invitation that day was accepted.
tiers.test: to be dragged into things you hate and lose the whole day.
tiers.stop: Do not check how you are doing while you are doing it.

tiers.do: Tell someone what you actually think when asked.
tiers.why: Honest, kind, and not softened into meaninglessness.
tiers.alt: Give one unsoftened honest opinion today.
tiers.when: someone next asks me how I am
tiers.open: Say what you actually think, without the softening clause.
tiers.done: your honest view was given, unsoftened, when asked for.
tiers.test: them to be hurt, and for honesty to have cost you something.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Reconnect with someone you fell out of contact with over a year ago.
tiers.why: A year of silence is easier to break than you have decided.
tiers.alt: Contact one person you have not spoken to in over a year.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Open the contact you have not used in a year and write one line.
tiers.done: contact is made with someone you had not spoken to in over a year.
tiers.test: them to be cold, or to not remember why they stopped replying.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "It has been a long time. I have been thinking about you. How are things?"

tiers.do: Sit with someone in difficulty and do not try to fix it.
tiers.why: Presence without solutions. Harder than advice, worth more.
tiers.alt: Listen to someone's problem without offering a single fix.
tiers.when: I am next alone with someone I know
tiers.open: Sit down and say nothing useful.
tiers.done: you sat with it and offered no solution.
tiers.test: the silence to be unbearable and for you to fill it with advice.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.
tiers.say: "That sounds really hard. I am not going to try and fix it."

tiers.do: Make a new acquaintance and see them a second time.
tiers.why: The second meeting is where acquaintance becomes possible friend.
tiers.alt: Arrange a second meeting with someone you recently met.
tiers.when: I next unlock my phone and see an unread message
tiers.open: Message the new person about a specific second thing.
tiers.done: you have seen the same new person twice.
tiers.test: them to decline the second time and for the first to have been politeness.
tiers.stop: Do not write it and sit on it. Send the first version.
tiers.say: "I enjoyed that. Are you about next week?"

tiers.do: Speak up for someone else out loud.
tiers.why: Advocacy costs standing. Spend some.
tiers.alt: Defend or support someone publicly, in the moment.
tiers.when: I next see someone whose face I recognise
tiers.open: Say it in the moment, out loud, in front of whoever is there.
tiers.done: you spoke up for someone else while it was still happening.
tiers.test: the room to turn on you, and for you to have made it worse for them.
tiers.stop: No softening clause at the end. Stop talking after the ask.

tiers.do: Ask for what you want without hedging or apologising first.
tiers.why: Notice the urge to soften it. Do not.
tiers.alt: Make one direct request with no preamble.
tiers.when: someone next asks me how I am
tiers.open: Make the request. Stop at the full stop.
tiers.done: the ask was made with no hedge in front and nothing softening behind.
